title: 2 Samuel Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 16.

questions.question: Who met King David when he was a little past the top of the hill?
options: Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth
Shimei, son of Gera
Abishai, son of Zeruiah
Hushai the Archite
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:1 states that Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, met David when he was a little past the top of the hill.

questions.question: What was Ziba carrying with him when he met King David?
options: Two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine
A sword and shield for protection
Gold and silver coins
A message from Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: Two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:1 describes Ziba bringing two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

questions.question: According to Ziba, what were the asses for?
options: For the king's household to ride on
To carry weapons
To bring water
To be sold in the market
questions.correctAnswer: For the king's household to ride on
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 16:2, Ziba explains that the asses are for the king's household to ride on.

questions.question: What did Ziba say the bread and summer fruit were for?
options: For the young men to eat
For the king's servants
For the enemy soldiers
For the elders of the city
questions.correctAnswer: For the young men to eat
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:2 records Ziba saying the bread and summer fruit were for the young men to eat.

questions.question: Where did Ziba say Mephibosheth's son was staying?
options: At Jerusalem
With King David
In the wilderness
In Gath
questions.correctAnswer: At Jerusalem
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 16:3, Ziba tells the king that Mephibosheth's son is abiding at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Mephibosheth's son say would happen that day?
options: The house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father
He would join King David's army
He would flee the city
He would make peace with Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:3 quotes Mephibosheth's son saying that the house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father that day.

questions.question: What did King David say to Ziba regarding Mephibosheth's property?
options: Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth
Return everything to Mephibosheth's son
Keep only the asses and bread
Give it to Abishai
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:4 shows David telling Ziba that all that pertained to Mephibosheth belonged to Ziba.

questions.question: Who came out from the family of Saul to curse King David?
options: Shimei, the son of Gera
Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth
Ahithophel
Hushai the Archite
questions.correctAnswer: Shimei, the son of Gera
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:5 identifies Shimei, son of Gera, from the family of Saul, as the one who came out to curse David.

questions.question: What did Shimei do as he cursed David?
options: He cast stones at David and his servants
He sang a song
He offered David food
He prayed for David
questions.correctAnswer: He cast stones at David and his servants
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:6 states that Shimei cast stones at David and all his servants.

questions.question: What name did Shimei use to insult David?
options: Man of Belial
Son of Jesse
King of Israel
Servant of Saul
questions.correctAnswer: Man of Belial
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:7 records Shimei calling David 'thou man of Belial' as he cursed him.

questions.question: True or False: Abishai wanted to kill Shimei for cursing King David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:9 shows Abishai asking the king for permission to kill Shimei because he cursed David.

questions.question: True or False: King David immediately allowed Abishai to kill Shimei.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:10 shows David refusing Abishai's request and telling him to let Shimei curse because the LORD had told him to do so.

questions.question: True or False: David believed the LORD might look on his affliction and reward him for Shimei's cursing.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:12 records David hoping that the LORD will look on his affliction and requite him good for Shimei's cursing.

questions.question: True or False: Shimei only cursed David but did not throw stones or dust at him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:13 states that Shimei cursed David, threw stones at him, and cast dust as they went by.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 16, which event comes first?
options: Ziba meeting David with provisions
Abishai asking to kill Shimei
David being cursed by Shimei
Absalom entering Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba meeting David with provisions
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 16:1-4 records Ziba meeting David first, before Shimei curses David (verse 5) or Abishai requests to kill Shimei (verse 9), and before Absalom enters Jerusalem (verse 15).

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Abishai's reaction to Shimei cursing King David, and what did he want to do?
options: He wanted to ignore Shimei's curses
He wanted to take off Shimei's head
He wanted to reason with Shimei
He encouraged David to flee
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to take off Shimei's head
questions.explanation: Abishai called Shimei a 'dead dog' and asked the king for permission to kill him (2 Samuel 16:9). This shows Abishai's protective zeal for David.

questions.question: How did King David respond to Abishai's desire to kill Shimei?
options: He commanded Abishai to kill Shimei immediately
He told Abishai to let Shimei curse because the LORD had told him to
He ignored Abishai's request
He asked Shimei to apologize
questions.correctAnswer: He told Abishai to let Shimei curse because the LORD had told him to
questions.explanation: David said that Shimei's cursing was allowed because the LORD had instructed it, emphasizing submission to God's will (2 Samuel 16:10).

questions.question: What reason did David give for allowing Shimei to continue cursing him?
options: Because Shimei was a close friend
Because the LORD had bidden him to allow it
Because David did not hear the curses
Because the servants demanded it
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had bidden him to allow it
questions.explanation: David explained that even his own son sought his life, so a Benjamite like Shimei cursing him was expected; he must let it be as the LORD had commanded (2 Samuel 16:11).

questions.question: What hope did David express regarding the curses he was receiving?
options: That the curses would stop soon
That the LORD would look on his affliction and reward him
That Shimei would be punished
That his servants would defend him
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD would look on his affliction and reward him
questions.explanation: David expressed hope that God would see his suffering and repay him good for the cursing he endured that day (2 Samuel 16:12).

questions.question: How does David's response to Shimei's cursing demonstrate the Christian virtue of humility?
options: By seeking revenge immediately
By submitting to God's will and refraining from retaliation
By ignoring the curses altogether
By hiding from his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By submitting to God's will and refraining from retaliation
questions.explanation: David chose to endure insults patiently because he recognized God's sovereign plan, exemplifying humility and trust (2 Samuel 16:9-12).

questions.question: What was Shimei doing as David and his men traveled by?
options: Offering food and water
Cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust
Praying for David
Singing praises
questions.correctAnswer: Cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust
questions.explanation: Shimei actively insulted David while throwing stones and dust at him as they passed (2 Samuel 16:13).

questions.question: What did David and his people do after traveling through the area where Shimei cursed them?
options: Engaged in battle
Rested and refreshed themselves
Followed Shimei to confront him
Returned to Jerusalem immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Rested and refreshed themselves
questions.explanation: The king and all the people were weary and took time to refresh themselves after their journey (2 Samuel 16:14).

questions.question: What significant event happened when Absalom and the men of Israel came to Jerusalem?
options: David regained his throne
Ahithophel joined Absalom
Shimei was crowned king
Hushai fled the city
questions.correctAnswer: Ahithophel joined Absalom
questions.explanation: Absalom arrived in Jerusalem with the men of Israel and was accompanied by Ahithophel, who was his counselor (2 Samuel 16:15).

questions.question: How did Hushai greet Absalom when he came to him?
options: He criticized Absalom's actions
He said, 'God save the king, God save the king'
He refused to speak to Absalom
He offered him gifts
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'God save the king, God save the king'
questions.explanation: Hushai greeted Absalom with blessings for the king's safety, showing outward loyalty (2 Samuel 16:16).

questions.question: What was Absalom's reaction to Hushai's greeting?
options: He was pleased and trusted Hushai
He questioned Hushai's kindness and loyalty
He ignored Hushai
He sent Hushai away
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned Hushai's kindness and loyalty
questions.explanation: Absalom asked why Hushai was not more supportive and why he had not accompanied him, doubting his friendship (2 Samuel 16:17).

questions.question: How did Hushai explain his loyalty to Absalom?
options: He pledged to serve only Absalom
He said he would serve whoever the LORD and people chose
He refused to serve anyone
He claimed neutrality
questions.correctAnswer: He said he would serve whoever the LORD and people chose
questions.explanation: Hushai expressed submission to God's will and loyalty to the chosen king, whether David or Absalom (2 Samuel 16:18).

questions.question: What argument did Hushai give for serving Absalom in his father's presence?
options: He wanted to betray David
He had always served Absalom's father and would do the same for Absalom
He was forced by Absalom to serve
He sought personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: He had always served Absalom's father and would do the same for Absalom
questions.explanation: Hushai said he served David and would likewise serve Absalom as he was now in his presence (2 Samuel 16:19).

questions.question: What counsel did Ahithophel give to Absalom to strengthen his position?
options: To attack David immediately
To go in unto David's concubines publicly
To seek peace with David
To flee Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: To go in unto David's concubines publicly
questions.explanation: Ahithophel advised Absalom to publicly sleep with David's concubines to show he was despised by his father and solidify his claim (2 Samuel 16:21).

questions.question: What was the effect of Ahithophel's counsel according to the chapter?
options: It was ignored
It was as if one consulted the oracle of God
It caused division among Israel
It led to immediate peace
questions.correctAnswer: It was as if one consulted the oracle of God
questions.explanation: Ahithophel's advice was highly esteemed and considered divinely inspired both by David and Absalom (2 Samuel 16:23).

questions.question: True or False: David permitted Shimei's cursing because he believed it was God's will for him to endure it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David explicitly said the LORD had told Shimei to curse him and thus he allowed it (2 Samuel 16:10-11).

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 16.

questions.question: What reason does Hushai give Absalom for not joining David, his friend?
options: He prefers to serve Absalom as the LORD and people have chosen him
He fears David will be defeated
He wants to spy for David in Absalom’s court
He is uncertain about the outcome of the rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: He prefers to serve Absalom as the LORD and people have chosen him
questions.explanation: Hushai tells Absalom that he will abide with him because the LORD, the people, and Israel have chosen Absalom, showing loyalty to the current chosen king rather than his personal friendship (2 Samuel 16:18).

questions.question: What was Ahithophel’s counsel to Absalom to strengthen his position among the people?
options: To go into his father's concubines publicly
To immediately attack David's forces
To seek peace with the elders of Israel
To imprison Hushai for betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: To go into his father's concubines publicly
questions.explanation: Ahithophel advised Absalom to publicly take his father's concubines to demonstrate that David had rejected him, which would strengthen Absalom’s support (2 Samuel 16:21).

questions.question: How is the counsel of Ahithophel described in terms of its reliability and divine inspiration?
options: As if a man had enquired at the oracle of God
As foolish and misguided
As a reflection of popular opinion
As inspired by foreign gods
questions.correctAnswer: As if a man had enquired at the oracle of God
questions.explanation: The text states Ahithophel’s counsel was so wise and trusted that it was as if one had asked an oracle of God, indicating its deep respect and reliability (2 Samuel 16:23).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently illustrated by Ahithophel’s counsel being equated to an oracle of God?
options: Simile
Metaphor
Chiasm
Irony
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: The comparison 'as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God' is a simile, a literary device using 'as' to compare Ahithophel’s counsel to divine oracular insight (2 Samuel 16:23).

questions.question: Why did David allow Shimei to curse him without retaliation?
options: Because the LORD had told Shimei to curse David
David was too weak to respond
Shimei was a close relative
David wanted to avoid bloodshed at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had told Shimei to curse David
questions.explanation: David stated that he must allow Shimei to curse him since the LORD had told Shimei to do so, implying divine permission or purpose behind it (2 Samuel 16:10).

questions.question: Which servant brought provisions to David as he was leaving the hill, and what did he claim about his master’s son?
options: Ziba; that Mephibosheth’s son remained in Jerusalem expecting restoration
Hushai; that David’s enemies planned to ambush him
Ahithophel; that Absalom was gathering strength
Shimei; that the house of Saul was cursed
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba; that Mephibosheth’s son remained in Jerusalem expecting restoration
questions.explanation: Ziba met David with provisions and told him that Mephibosheth’s son was in Jerusalem, expecting the kingdom to be restored to him (2 Samuel 16:1-3).

questions.question: What was the cultural significance of Absalom publicly taking his father’s concubines according to ancient Near Eastern royal customs?
options: It was a public claim to the throne and an assertion of dominance
It was a sign of reconciliation with his father
It indicated a religious ceremony of blessing
It was a way to punish the concubines
questions.correctAnswer: It was a public claim to the throne and an assertion of dominance
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, a son publicly taking his father’s concubines was a symbolic act asserting his claim to the throne and signaling the father's rejection (2 Samuel 16:21-22).

questions.question: How does the theme of divine sovereignty appear in David’s response to Shimei’s cursing?
options: David acknowledges that the LORD controls even curses against him
David curses Shimei back invoking God's wrath
David ignores the curse and seeks revenge immediately
David leaves the scene to avoid confrontation
questions.correctAnswer: David acknowledges that the LORD controls even curses against him
questions.explanation: David accepts Shimei’s cursing as permitted by the LORD, showing his submission to divine sovereignty over human affairs (2 Samuel 16:10-12).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of a servant bringing provisions to a fleeing king, similar to Ziba’s role here?
options: 1 Samuel 30:11-12
Genesis 37:28
Exodus 3:1
Judges 6:15
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 30:11-12
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 30:11-12, a servant brings provisions to David when he flees from enemies, paralleling Ziba’s provision of bread, fruit, and wine to David (2 Samuel 16:1-2).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew term translated as 'man of Belial' used by Shimei suggest about his accusation against David?
options: It denotes a worthless or wicked man
It means a righteous leader
It implies a wise counselor
It indicates a foreign king
questions.correctAnswer: It denotes a worthless or wicked man
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Belial' means 'worthlessness' or 'wickedness,' so calling David a 'man of Belial' was a strong insult accusing him of being evil or worthless (2 Samuel 16:7).

questions.question: True or False: Abishai wanted to kill Shimei immediately to defend King David's honor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Abishai asked the king for permission to kill Shimei, calling him a 'dead dog' and wanting to defend David’s honor (2 Samuel 16:9).

questions.question: True or False: Hushai declares that he will serve only the LORD and reject both David and Absalom.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hushai declares loyalty to whichever king the LORD and the people choose, specifically Absalom at that moment, not rejecting both (2 Samuel 16:18).

questions.question: What theme from Psalms is reflected in David’s acceptance of Shimei’s cursing?
options: The righteous sufferer who trusts in God's justice
The victorious king over his enemies
The joyful worshipper in the temple
The lawgiver who instructs the people
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous sufferer who trusts in God's justice
questions.explanation: David’s acceptance of suffering and cursing while trusting the LORD’s justice reflects the righteous sufferer theme found in Psalms like Psalm 3 and Psalm 7 (2 Samuel 16:10-12).

questions.question: What was the strategic importance of Hushai’s presence in Absalom’s court after David fled?
options: To act as a spy for David and counter Ahithophel’s counsel
To genuinely serve Absalom and betray David
To negotiate peace between David and Absalom
To rally the people against Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: To act as a spy for David and counter Ahithophel’s counsel
questions.explanation: Though Hushai claims loyalty to Absalom, he was actually a spy for David, appointed earlier to counter Ahithophel’s advice (2 Samuel 16:16-19; see 2 Samuel 15:32-37).

questions.question: How does the event of Absalom taking his father’s concubines foreshadow later biblical themes of rebellion and judgment?
options: It symbolizes broken covenant and the consequences of rebellion against God’s anointed
It foreshadows the Messiah’s birth
It illustrates the establishment of a new covenant
It represents a peaceful transfer of power
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes broken covenant and the consequences of rebellion against God’s anointed
questions.explanation: Absalom’s act is a public declaration of rebellion and rejection of David, God’s anointed king, symbolizing covenant breach and divine judgment themes developed throughout Scripture (2 Samuel 16:21-22).

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by David's acceptance of Shimei's curses without retaliation?
options: The doctrine of divine sovereignty and submission to God's will
The doctrine of predestination excluding human responsibility
The doctrine of immediate divine retribution
The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine sovereignty and submission to God's will
questions.explanation: David allows Shimei to curse him because he acknowledges that the LORD has permitted it (2 Samuel 16:10-11). This demonstrates the doctrine that God’s sovereign will governs even human actions and suffering, and believers are to submit to God's providence. See also Romans 8:28.

questions.question: What does the provision of bread, raisins, summer fruits, and wine by Ziba to David symbolize in a theological context?
options: God's sustaining grace for the weary in spiritual journeys
The necessity of ritual sacrifice for forgiveness
The exclusivity of the monarchy's power
The establishment of a new covenant through David
questions.correctAnswer: God's sustaining grace for the weary in spiritual journeys
questions.explanation: Ziba's provision is meant to sustain those faint in the wilderness (2 Samuel 16:1-2), typifying God's grace that sustains believers during spiritual hardships and trials. This echoes God’s provision in the wilderness for Israel (Exodus 16).

questions.question: How does Absalom’s act of publicly taking his father's concubines relate to the broader biblical narrative of sin and rebellion?
options: It symbolizes a usurpation of authority and a break in covenantal loyalty
It signifies the initiation of a new priestly line
It represents the fulfillment of a messianic prophecy
It demonstrates the restoration of the Davidic covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a usurpation of authority and a break in covenantal loyalty
questions.explanation: Absalom’s public act (2 Samuel 16:21-22) is a political and symbolic declaration of rebellion against David, representing a serious breach of covenantal faithfulness and authority, reflecting humanity's sin of rejecting God's appointed rule. See also Psalm 2:1-3.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God permitting Shimei to curse David?
options: God’s justice in allowing consequences for sin
God’s patience and long-suffering with His people
God’s omnipotence in directing events according to His plan
God’s wrath against rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence in directing events according to His plan
questions.explanation: God's permission of Shimei's cursing (2 Samuel 16:10) shows His sovereign control over human actions, underscoring divine omnipotence in orchestrating history for His purposes. See Isaiah 46:10.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about human sinfulness and its consequences is reflected in Shimei’s accusations against David?
options: The doctrine of original sin and its perpetuation through bloodshed
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
The doctrine of sanctification through works
The doctrine of election excluding sinners
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of original sin and its perpetuation through bloodshed
questions.explanation: Shimei calls David a 'bloody man' (2 Samuel 16:7-8), indicting him for shedding blood and perpetuating sin, reflecting the biblical teaching that sin has deep consequences and affects all humanity. See Romans 3:23.

questions.question: How does Hushai's declared loyalty to Absalom despite being David's friend illustrate a theological theme related to human allegiance?
options: The complexity of human loyalty in the face of divine sovereignty
The necessity of absolute loyalty only to God
The rejection of political authority in favor of spiritual authority
The fulfillment of prophecy concerning betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: The complexity of human loyalty in the face of divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: Hushai claims loyalty to Absalom based on the people's choice (2 Samuel 16:17-19), illustrating the human tension between personal allegiance and recognition of divine providence in leadership, highlighting the complexity of loyalty amid God's sovereign plans.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative is foreshadowed by David’s suffering and rejection by his own son, Absalom?
options: The suffering servant motif ultimately fulfilled in Christ
The establishment of the Mosaic Law
The exile and restoration of Israel
The conquest of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: The suffering servant motif ultimately fulfilled in Christ
questions.explanation: David’s rejection and suffering at Absalom’s hands (2 Samuel 16:15-22) foreshadow the suffering servant theme, typologically pointing to Christ’s rejection and sacrifice for redemption, as described in Isaiah 53.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's allowance of evil acts, such as Shimei's cursing of David, contradicts His goodness. What does 2 Samuel 16:5-13 actually teach about God's providence and human sin?
options: God permits human sin within His sovereign plan, using it to fulfill His purposes
God directly commands all evil acts without exception
God is unaware of human actions and thus cannot prevent evil
God punishes all evil immediately upon its occurrence
questions.correctAnswer: God permits human sin within His sovereign plan, using it to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: David’s acceptance of Shimei’s cursing (2 Samuel 16:5-13) shows that God sovereignly permits even sinful acts, using them to accomplish His redemptive plan, demonstrating both His providence and justice. See also Romans 8:28.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do verses 10 and 11 convey about divine permission and human responsibility?
options: God’s sovereign permission does not negate human accountability
God controls actions but exempts humans from judgment
Humans have free will but God is not involved in their choices
God’s sovereignty removes the need for human obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign permission does not negate human accountability
questions.explanation: David acknowledges that the LORD has permitted Shimei's cursing (2 Samuel 16:10-11), showing God's sovereign control; yet the question 'Who shall say why?' implies human responsibility remains, teaching the compatibility of divine sovereignty and human accountability.

questions.question: How does Ahithophel’s counsel to Absalom to publicly sin against David’s concubines reveal the nature of sin’s destructive power within covenant relationships?
options: It demonstrates how sin attacks the foundation of covenant loyalty and unity
It reveals that sin can be used righteously in political power struggles
It shows that sin is less significant when done publicly
It teaches that covenant relationships are irrelevant to political authority
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates how sin attacks the foundation of covenant loyalty and unity
questions.explanation: Ahithophel’s advice (2 Samuel 16:21) to violate David’s concubines publicly is a strategic move to destroy the unity and loyalty central to the covenant community, illustrating sin’s corrosive effect on God-ordained relationships.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the description of Ahithophel’s counsel as being as if ‘a man had enquired at the oracle of God’?
options: God’s wisdom and the seriousness of counsel given
God’s mercy and forgiveness
God’s omnipresence in all places
God’s wrath against disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom and the seriousness of counsel given
questions.explanation: The text (2 Samuel 16:23) attributes to Ahithophel’s counsel a divine-like wisdom, reflecting that God’s wisdom is supreme and that counsel resembling divine oracles carries grave significance and authority.

questions.question: What combined insight about God’s providence and human suffering is revealed through verses 12 and 13?
options: God sees human affliction and may reward endurance amid suffering
God causes suffering arbitrarily without purpose
Human suffering indicates God’s abandonment
God advocates for immediate revenge against oppressors
questions.correctAnswer: God sees human affliction and may reward endurance amid suffering
questions.explanation: David expresses hope that the LORD will look upon his affliction and repay good for the cursing (2 Samuel 16:12-13), teaching that God is aware of suffering and can bring blessing through endurance, consistent with biblical teaching on sanctification. See James 1:12.

questions.question: How does the encounter between David and Ziba in verses 1-4 illustrate a theological tension regarding loyalty and human motives?
options: It shows that human actions can be motivated by self-interest even in godly contexts
It proves that all servants of God are always loyal
It teaches that material provision guarantees spiritual blessing
It indicates that God blesses only those who possess wealth
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that human actions can be motivated by self-interest even in godly contexts
questions.explanation: Ziba's presentation of provisions and claim that Mephibosheth's son is disloyal (2 Samuel 16:1-4) reveals human self-interest and deception, demonstrating the biblical reality of sinful motives amid appearances of loyalty.

questions.question: What broader narrative arc does the arrival of Ahithophel with Absalom in Jerusalem signify in the context of Israel’s history?
options: The escalation of civil rebellion threatening the Davidic covenant
The fulfillment of the Exodus from Egypt
The inauguration of the Levitical priesthood
The immediate restoration of Israel’s monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: The escalation of civil rebellion threatening the Davidic covenant
questions.explanation: Ahithophel's joining Absalom in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 16:15) marks the intensification of rebellion that challenges David's divinely established kingship, threatening God's covenant with David and Israel’s future, a key moment in the redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined theological lesson is drawn from verses 9 and 11 regarding human zeal and divine patience?
options: Zeal for God's honor must be tempered by submission to His will
Human zeal overrides God’s sovereign plans
Divine patience justifies ignoring injustice
Zeal guarantees immediate divine approval
questions.correctAnswer: Zeal for God's honor must be tempered by submission to His will
questions.explanation: Abishai’s desire to kill Shimei (2 Samuel 16:9) contrasts with David’s restraint (verse 11), teaching that even justified zeal must submit to God’s sovereign permission and timing, highlighting divine patience and human obedience. See Ecclesiastes 7:8.
